phase_name: Part B -- Emit the Premise Re-Validation Block

objectives.description: Emit bounded premise-re-validation block keyed to six trigger shapes, gated on prior artifact existence
Reuse an existing cheap idiom rather than inventing a second mechanism
Emit claims and a pointer only; no conflict detection
Add fixtures in both directions to test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh

approaches_tried.approach: Literal reuse of the sha256sum description_fingerprint/supersession comparison for premise re-validation
approaches_tried.reason: that idiom detects whether a RECORDED past description matches the CURRENT one; no prior artifact in this codebase records a fingerprint of a premise it measured against, so there is nothing to compare a current fingerprint to. Substituted a grep-based lexical extraction over the six trigger-class shapes instead -- cheaper than hashing, no new semantic mechanism, same no-new-measurement spirit.

deviations.description: Reuse the existing fingerprint-and-supersession idiom in that same function rather than inventing a second mechanism
deviations.reason: The sha256sum fingerprint/supersession idiom has no analogue for premise re-validation (no prior artifact records a fingerprint to compare against). Reused the idiom's spirit (no new measurement, a single cheap check, byte-identical-when-absent) via grep-based lexical extraction instead of a literal sha256sum reuse.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered -- see Phase 7's Task list for the full reasoning)*

notes: Added a premise-re-validation code block to orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh, inserted immediately after the existing prior_decisions_block logic and before the dispatch-file write section: detects whether this task directory already holds at least one report/plan/summary *.md file (prior_artifact_list array), and if so, greps the description for lines matching any of the six Carried-Figure-Discipline trigger-class lexical signatures (N-of-M ratio, exit/PASS/FAIL/gateN, always/never/cannot/is-required, numeric-unit counts). When both conditions hold, emits a '## Premise Re-Validation' section listing the prior artifact paths, the extracted claim lines, and a pointer to report-format.md's 'The premise a dispatch acts on' subsection -- never any judgment about whether the claims are still accurate (no conflict detection, per Phase 6's exclusion). Added Group 22 to test-orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh with three cases: (a) prior artifact present + trigger-laden description -> section present, names both prior artifact paths, extracted claims present, pointer present, no adjudication language; (b) no prior artifact + same trigger-laden description -> section completely absent; (c) prior artifact present + non-trigger description -> section completely absent. All 193 suite cases pass (up from 183 before this phase), including every pre-existing Group 1-21 case unchanged, which is itself strong byte-identity evidence for the common (non-triggering) case. Found and fixed two bugs during fixture authoring: the pointer text in the emitted block had been wrapped across two echo lines splitting the phrase 'The premise a dispatch acts on', failing a substring assertion -- rewrapped onto a single echo call; and a test assertion incorrectly expected the extracted claim text to be absent from the WHOLE dispatch file in the no-prior-artifact case, when in fact the unconditional '## Description' section always echoes the raw description verbatim regardless -- removed that over-broad assertion since the section-absence check already covers the real requirement. bash -n and shellcheck clean on both files (same pre-existing info-level findings only, no new ones).
